draft.title: Magnetic flux
card: Magnetic flux is the amount of magnetic field passing through an area. It is measured in webers (Wb).
Φ = BA cos θ. B is the magnetic field strength in tesla, and A is the area of the loop in square metres.
θ is the angle between the magnetic field and the normal, a line at right angles to the surface of the loop. It is not the angle between the field and the surface.
Flux is greatest when the field is along the normal (θ = 0°, cos θ = 1). It is zero when the field runs parallel to the surface (θ = 90°, cos θ = 0).
draft.remember: Flux depends on field strength, area and the angle between the field and the normal.

a.q: A flat coil sits in a uniform magnetic field. Which change to the coil would reduce the flux through it to zero?
opts: Turning it until the field runs parallel to its surface
Turning it until the field is along its normal
Doubling the area of the coil
Doubling the strength of the field
a.why: Flux is zero when cos θ = 0, which happens at θ = 90°. This is when the field runs parallel to the surface. Turning the coil so the field is along the normal gives the greatest flux, not zero, because the angle is then 0°.
a.clue: Zero flux means no field lines pass through the surface.

b.q: A square loop of side 0.20 m sits in a uniform 0.50 T field. The field is at 60° to the normal of the loop. What is the flux through the loop?
b.why: A = 0.20 × 0.20 = 0.040 m². Φ = 0.50 × 0.040 × cos 60° = 0.010 Wb. Using 60° as the angle to the surface instead would give cos 30° and a wrong answer of 0.017 Wb.
b.clue: The angle in the formula is measured from the normal, and cos 60° = 0.5.

a.best: Turning it until the field runs parallel to its surface
